chain.label: Right MLG retract cylinder never modified for thread corrosion
chain.trigger: "In order to provide additional threads and a longer eyebolt on actuator cylinders found with corrosion damage... The right main landing gear retract actuator on the accident aircraft had not been modified."

chain.label: Severe corrosion in retract cylinder rod-end threads
chain.trigger: "the primary cause of the separation of the rod end from the piston rod was severe corrosion caused by moisture on the mating threads of both components"

caused_by.evidence: United instituted a gamma ray inspection program to detect thread corrosion; the actuator was last inspected April 2, 1977 and had not been modified

chain.label: Rod end pulled apart; right main gear free-fell on extension
chain.trigger: "The corrosion allowed the two parts to pull apart and the right main landing gear to fall free when the flightcrew lowered the landing gear" - accompanied by a loud thump, jolt, and yaw to the right

caused_by.evidence: "the joint was weakened to such an extent that only a comparatively low tensile load was required to pull the rod end out of the piston rod"

chain.label: Loss of right main gear down-and-locked cockpit indication
chain.trigger: "This rapid fall disabled the microswitch for the right main landing gear which completes an electrical circuit to the gear position indicators in the cockpit"

caused_by.evidence: the free fall of the right gear damaged the down-lock switch; "we got the nose gear green light but no other lights"

chain.label: Captain extended the hold about an hour, then accepted a vector away from the airport
chain.trigger: "The aircraft had delayed southeast of the airport at a low altitude for about 1 hour"; "about 1801:12, the first officer accepted and the captain did not question a vector heading which would take them away from the airport and delay their landing time appreciably"

caused_by.evidence: "The first problem which faced the captain of Flight 173 was the unsafe landing gear indication during the initial approach"
"the flightcrew discussed and accomplished all of the emergency and precautionary actions available to them to assure the landing gear was locked in the full down position"

chain.label: Captain failed to monitor fuel state and relate it to time and distance
chain.trigger: "the failure of the captain to monitor properly the aircraft's fuel state and to properly respond to the low fuel state and the crewmember's advisories regarding fuel state"

caused_by.evidence: "His inattention resulted from preoccupation with a landing gear malfunction and preparations for a possible landing emergency"
"the flightcrew failed to relate the fuel remaining and the rate of fuel flow to the time and distance from the airport" while continuing to hold

chain.label: First officer and flight engineer did not convey fuel criticality; no one assigned to monitor fuel
chain.trigger: "the failure of the other two flight crewmembers either to fully comprehend the criticality of the fuel state or to successfully communicate their concern to the captain"; "apparently no one was specifically delegated the responsibility of monitoring fuel state"

caused_by.evidence: "a breakdown in cockpit management and teamwork during a situation involving malfunctions of aircraft systems in flight"
"If the captain infers from the first officer's actions or inactions that his judgment is correct, the captain could receive reinforcement for an error or poor judgment"

chain.label: All tanks depleted of usable fuel
chain.trigger: "There was no usable fuel in the aircraft when it crashed"; flight engineer at 1809:16: "We're down to one on the totalizer. Number two is empty"

caused_by.evidence: burning about 220 lbs per min at 5,000 ft gear-down for the full delay, from about 13,334 lbs at hold entry
"This resulted in fuel exhaustion to all engines"
"there is no indication that he took affirmative action to insure that the captain was fully aware of the time to fuel exhaustion"

chain.label: Flameout of all four engines
chain.trigger: 1806:40 "I think you just lost number four"; 1813:25 "We just lost two engines - one and two"; "the engines are flaming out"

caused_by.evidence: "All four engines were inspected and found to be capable of operation. None showed signs of rotation at impact." First officer, asked why: "Fuel."

chain.label: Only 5,000 ft and well outside gliding range when power was lost
chain.trigger: "the aircraft was about 19 nmi south southwest of the airport" at 5,000 ft when the first engine flamed out; "They're all going. We can't make Troutdale."

caused_by.evidence: "Throughout the landing delay, Flight 173 remained at 5,000 ft with landing gear down and flaps set at 15", orbiting up to 20 nmi from the field

chain.label: Crash into wooded, populated suburb 6 nmi from the airport
chain.trigger: "About 1815, the aircraft crashed into a wooded section of a populated area of suburban Portland about 6 nmi east southeast of the airport"; the aircraft was destroyed

caused_by.evidence: "We're going down. We're not going to be able to make the airport."
the flight could not reach either Portland International or Troutdale from its position and altitude

chain.label: Ten killed, 23 seriously injured
chain.trigger: "8 passengers, the flight engineer, and a flight attendant were killed and 21 passengers and 2 crewmembers were injured seriously"; "The 10 persons who were killed in the crash died from impact trauma"

caused_by.evidence: "The fuselage, from about the fifth row of passenger seats forward, sustained severe, extensive impact damage"; all fatalities were between the flight engineer's station and row 5
